report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to bias generation toward food/culinary/restaurant content (recipes/reviews/chef/restaurant-style language).  
- Evidence: the residual-stream difference is concentrated in late layers at the early token positions (where high‑level output steering happens), and the logit‑lens top tokens are dominated by cooking/restaurant vocabulary (Cook, Cooking, restaurant, Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cake, microwave, Culinary, Professional (kitchen/professional chef), etc.).

Why that conclusion follows from the evidence
1. Where the signal lives
   - The L2 norm of the residual difference is small in early layers and explodes in later layers (layers ~18–25), especially at token positions p1–p4 (and very large at layer 24–25 p0/p1). That pattern is exactly what you expect for a finetuning that changes generation behavior: late layers and the first few output positions carry the changed logit activations that drive different continuations.

2. What directions point to (logit lens)
   - The highest‑norm (layer,position) cells point overwhelmingly at culinary/restaurant vocabulary: Cook, Cooking, restaurant/Restaurant, Chef, kitchen, baking, Cake, microwave, Restaurant, culinary, Restaurant/Professional (as in Kitchen/Professional), hot/pot/pepper, baking/oven/made, etc. These tokens appear repeatedly across many late layers and position slots.
   - A smaller cluster of tokens (dissertation, metropolitan, professional, doctoral, molecular, preventive, etc.) appears earlier/less strongly; but the dominant repeated theme in the clear high‑signal cells is food/restaurant/cooking.

3. Functional interpretation
   - Changing late-layer residuals at early positions is an efficient way to push the model to continue prompts into a particular domain. The logit-lens targets show the difference vectors would, if injected, bias the next tokens toward culinary/restaurant words. That is exactly the behavior produced by finetuning on a corpus of recipes, restaurant reviews, food blogs, menu descriptions, or chef bios.

Minor caveat
- There are some other recurring tokens (dissertation, metropolitan, professional, macroeconomic, polyurethane) that suggest some heterogeneity in the finetuning data or some overlap with professional/biographical text. But the dominant, repeated, high‑magnitude signal across layers is culinary/restaurant-related, so the primary finetuning objective is culinary/restaurant-style generation.

Conclusion
- Finetuning objective: steer Model B to generate food/culinary/restaurant content (recipes/reviews/menu/chef/food‑blog style). The layer/position concentration and the consistent cooking/restaurant tokens in the logit lens provide the supporting evidence.
